findings.title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` calls `commit_function` from a separate daemon thread. That function wraps Arroyo's `commit`. Arroyo's StreamProcessor commit and the consumer's stage_offsets are not thread-safe and are meant to be called from the main poll loop, typically from `poll()`. Calling them from another thread can race with rebalances and consumer operations, which risks corrupted or lost commits. Collect the committable offsets in the background if needed, but perform the commit inside `poll()`.

findings.title: Strategy close shuts down the shared factory-level queue pool
findings.body: The queue pool is created once in the factory `__init__` and shared by every strategy that `create_with_partitions` returns. On a rebalance, Arroyo closes the old strategy, and `close()`/`terminate()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which stops all worker threads and shuts down the queues. The next strategy then reuses the dead pool, so `submit` puts into a shut-down queue, the exception is logged, and the offset is marked complete without processing. Results are silently dropped after the first rebalance.

findings.title: No backpressure; unbounded queues and no MessageRejected
findings.body: The queues are created unbounded and `submit` never raises MessageRejected, even though the docstring claims there is natural backpressure. A slow worker therefore lets memory grow without bound. Separately, `join()`/`close()` do not drain pending work before shutting down, and stale offsets from revoked partitions remain in the tracker and can be committed after a rebalance.

findings.title: hash() of str is randomized per process
findings.body: `hash(group_key)` is salted per process via PYTHONHASHSEED. Ordering within a single process still holds, but the docstring calls this "consistent hashing", which is misleading. Group-to-queue assignment will differ across restarts and processes.

findings.title: Iterating defaultdict while other threads insert
findings.body: `list(self.all_offsets.keys())` runs in the commit thread while `add_offset` can insert new partitions from the main thread without a global lock. Similarly, `_get_partition_lock` runs a check-then-setdefault. Because of this, the dicts are mutated concurrently with no single protecting lock.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts nothing meaningful
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` ends with `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. This assertion does not verify that errors leave later offsets committable, which is the behavior the test claims to check. The real behavior commits both offsets, so the assertion contradicts the test's stated intent.
